newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Mainfreight confident of $5.5 mln yr net.
newsitem.headline: Mainfreight confident of $5.5 mln yr net.

text.p: Transport group Mainfreight Ltd said on Friday it was confident of meeting its prospectus forecast of a NZ$5.5 million net profit for the year to March 1997.
The company reported a first half net profit of NZ$2.01 million, up from $1.58 million a year earlier.
"This first half result reinforces the directors' confidence that the forecast earnings for the 1997 financial year as detailed in the May prospectus will be achieved," the company said.
Group net profit before float costs, taxation and minority interests was NZ$3.81 million, up 51.4 percent, on consolidated revenue of $69.38 million, up 7.8 percent.
Lep International (NZ) Limited, acquired in September, contributed NZ$5.6 million revenue and $193,000 profit before taxation. Float costs for the period were NZ$526,000 and are now complete.

"Improved margins in our forwarding activities combined with increased international revenues explain this large profit increase, however an allowance for last year's disappointing first half results should be made," the company said.
The warehousing division has seen a rise in Australian imports, reflecting the high exchange rate and favourable Trans Tasman shipping costs. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
